_README: Spoken overrides for terms the narrator gets wrong.
Key = the term as it appears in the devotional (case-insensitive, matched
on whole words). Value = what to SEND to the engine instead. The devotional
text is never altered; this only changes what the voice is handed.
WHY THIS IS HAND-MAINTAINED: pronunciation of Greek/Hebrew transliterations
cannot be verified automatically. The QA loop checks accuracy by
transcribing the render with Whisper and diffing it against the source, but
Whisper was not trained on these transliterations and mangles them whatever
the voice does ('eleos' comes back as 'ilios', 'diathekei' as 'diathek').
The gauge is broken for this one case, so these words are the only part of
the narration that needs a human ear.
MEASURED, so you do not have to rediscover it: the `pronunciation` field
already in the devotionals ('KHEH-sed', 'as-FAH-lay-ah') is NOT a drop-in

_LESSON: Hyphenated pseudo-phonetic respellings MAKE CHATTERBOX WORSE, measured 2026-08-19.
'bereshit bara Elohim' rendered at clarity 1.00 untouched. Overriding it to
'beh-ray-sheet bah-rah eh-loh-heem' produced 'ha ha ha bah ha ha himp lo himp'
at clarity 0.18-0.36 and burned all four attempts.
Two reasons it fails on BOTH sides of the loop: the engine reads hyphenated
syllables as literal fragments, and the QA gate then expects the RESPELLING in
the transcript, which Whisper will not produce either. An override here has to
be a real word the engine already says correctly - not a pronunciation guide.
Leave this empty rather than guessing.
